description: Flat per-scene shot list produced directly from the approved narration script (RFC 0008). Replaces the semantic visual-planning stack (episode_visual_model + explanation_plan + its critic/reviser/release loop) and the character stack entirely -- there are no on-screen characters, no dialogue, no lip-sync. Every scene is a single hand-drawn illustration under a deterministic camera move. There is no diagram vocabulary, no primitive/blueprint selection, and no model-authored geometry: the director chooses a camera move from a bounded enum and writes one concrete image prompt. Image prompts describe the real, particular thing being said -- never an abstract entity name -- because the prior system's prompts were built from diagram entity labels and produced illustrations that had nothing to do with the episode's actual subject.

image_prompt.description: ONE concrete, particular, physically depictable subject and what it is doing -- 'a tabby cat mid-fall, back arched, front half already twisted toward the floor'. Never an abstraction, never a diagram noun, never a restatement of the narration, never a label or any text to be drawn. The house style (faceless stick-figure humans, detailed environments/objects/animals, muted near-monochrome wash, wide off-centre compositions) is applied downstream via reference-image conditioning; do not describe style, palette, lighting or camera here.

camera_move.description: The deterministic move applied to the still. Vary it between consecutive scenes so cuts feel edited rather than mechanical.

on_screen_label.description: Optional and usually empty. At most a few words. The voice-over carries the story; text on screen competes with captions.
